releases.name: tasteskill v2.1.4
releases.body:
This release makes the inspector's browser profiles safe when several runs go at once ([#157](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/issues/157), [#158](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/158), [#159](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/159)). The rules of `design-taste-frontend` are unchanged; only `scripts/lib/cdp.mjs` changed.

- **Fix: one inspector run could delete the browser profile of another run that was still going.** Chrome keeps no `lockfile` on macOS and Linux, so the sweep added in 2.1.0 judged a profile unused by its age alone. A second run started during a long one could then pull that run's profile away. Thanks to @t4sh for the report and the fix.
- **Leftover profiles are cleaned up again, safely.** Every profile now carries `taste-skill-owner.json` with the machine and the process IDs of the run and its Chrome. A later run removes a profile left by a killed run only when that file names this machine and neither process is alive. A profile without the file is never touched.

Profiles left by earlier versions are not removed automatically. To clear them, delete the `ad-chrome-*` folders in your temp folder (or in `TASTE_SKILL_TMP`).

Update:

``

releases.name: tasteskill v2.1.2
releases.body:
Fixes [#151](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/issues/151): `design-taste-frontend` did not load in Claude Code. The skill description added in 2.1.0 contained an unquoted `: `, so its YAML frontmatter failed to parse and the skill was silently dropped ("Unknown skill"). Update to get it back:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

Claude Code plugin users: `/plugin update`.

So it cannot happen again, every `SKILL.md` frontmatter is now parsed with a strict YAML parser on each push and pull request (`tests/frontmatter.mjs`, `check-skills.yml`).

Thanks to @TofiBot for the precise report.

releases.name: tasteskill v2.1.1
releases.body:
One skill to reach for. Installing taste-skill no longer means an agent might pick an older skill for the job.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

## What changed

- **The classic skills are opt-in.** soft, minimalist, brutalist, gpt-taste, Stitch, v1 and v2-experimental run only when you call them by name (`/high-end-visual-design` in Claude Code, `$minimalist-ui` in Codex). An agent never picks one by itself.
- **Redesigns are part of taste-skill.** It records the existing page in a real browser first, keeps the stack, the content and everything that works, then changes type, colour, the frame, states and stock components in that order, and proves it with before-and-after screenshots. `redesign-existing-projects` is retired.
- **Image generation has its own repo:** [Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills) (`imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`, `image-to-code`), same install names.
- **`full-output-enforcement` is removed.**
- **Claude Code plugins:** `taste-skill@taste-skill` now carries only the default skill; the classics are `taste-s

releases.name: tasteskill v2.1
releases.body:
tasteskill v2.1 builds the screens people work in, not only the pages they read, and keeps every page's frame clean.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

The install name did not change. Needs Node 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. Installs nothing, uses no API keys.

## What is new

- **Dashboards and app screens.** The skill tells a page from an app screen. An app screen gets its own run: a style dealt from seven styles distilled from real product screens, a face taken from the brief, a shell, real data that adds up, charts that annotate what happened, every state, and its own checks (`inspect.mjs --app`). Ships with `assets/app.css` and `assets/charts.js`.
- **Product pages that show their app** build those screens by the same rules, so the hero's screenshot looks like a working product, not grey bars.
- **The frame of a page.** The inspector now fails the things readers name first when a page looks wrong: no clear title, margins that do not match, a section shoved to one side with half the screen empty, random blank stretches, untitled sections, text against the edge, a title that is not read

**Taste Skill** is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents design websites and app screens instead of assembling the average landing page. It gives the agent an art direction, real pictures and a way to check its own work in a real browser. Pages it has built, each from one brief:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0). ## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` That installs the skill with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. The skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium**. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Finding pictures needs network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so it does not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skill into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates it in place.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See [Moved skills](#moved-skills). ## How v2 works The skill is built from a study of 247 curated sites. A build runs in six steps: 1. Reads the brief and lists what only this client has. 2. A script deals three of 20 researched directions and the agent picks one. 3. Finds the idea: one sentence tying the client's own material to that direction. 4. Builds with real pictures and footage from open collections, credited. 5. Checks the page in a real browser at three widths and fails it on slop. 6. Looks at its own screenshots and fixes the top three problems, up to three rounds. A build takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens. Details are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the [study](skills/taste-skill/references/research.md). Dashboards and app screens (v2.1) take their own route: the skill deals one of the app styles distilled from real product screens, builds the shell, the data, the charts and the tables to those numbers, and checks the result with app rules: quiet panels, aligned figures, colour spent on data, a phone layout where the navigation folds away. A product's landing page builds the app it shows the same way, so its screenshots look like a working product. v2.1 also checks the frame of every page (a clear title on the first screen, equal margins, no section shoved to one side, no random blank stretches) and moves the way strong award sites do, measured on the latest 100 Awwwards Sites of the Day. ## Moved skills This repo holds one skill, `design-taste-frontend`. The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names: | Install name | Where it lives now | | --- | --- | | `high-end-visual-design`, `minimalist-ui`, `industrial-brutalist-ui`, `gpt-taste`, `stitch-design-taste`, `design-taste-frontend-v1`, `design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental` | **[Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics)** | | `imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`, `image-to-code` | **[Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills)** | | `redesign-existing-projects` | Part of `design-taste-frontend`, which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything | | `full-output-enforcement` | Removed. For the same problem, see **[Leonxlnx/unlazy](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy)** | Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill "high-end-visual-design" ``` ## Common Questions **What does the skill need?** Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. It installs nothing and uses no API keys. It needs the internet only to find pictures. **Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?** From open collections such as Wikimedia Commons, Openverse and the Met. Only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA files are offered, and the skill puts the credits on the page. Replace them with your own when you have them. **Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?** Yes. The rules are about design, not a framework. **Is it for dashboards and app screens?** Yes, since v2.1. The skill tells a page from an app screen and builds a dashboard, an admin view or a settings screen with its own run: a style dealt from a study of real product screens, quiet panels, honest data and charts, and its own checks (`inspect.mjs --app`). ## Support the project If Taste Skill helps you, consider sponsoring: [Sponsor on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/Leonxlnx) ### Open Source Supporters

aiSummary.oneLiner: An anti-slop frontend framework and skill set designed to prevent AI agents from generating generic, poorly designed UI.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Taste-Skill acts as an anti-slop frontend framework intended to elevate the design quality of code generated by AI agents. It addresses the common issue where LLMs produce generic, visually unappealing, or heavily boilerplate UIs by providing a curated set of design rules and constraints. The project functions as a specific 'skill' that can be injected into agentic workflows to guide styling, layout, and component choices. By enforcing strong design opinions and best practices, it ensures the resulting frontends look premium and bespoke rather than obviously machine-generated. It effectively gives the AI a sense of 'good taste' in modern web design.
keyFeatures: Anti-Slop Directives: Prevents the generation of generic, overused UI patterns and standard Bootstrap-style layouts.
Design Opinionation: Enforces strong, modern design principles regarding typography, spacing, and color palettes.
Agent Skill Integration: Designed to be easily consumed and executed by autonomous coding agents like Claude Code or Codex.
Premium Component Constraints: Guides the AI to use modern frontend techniques and minimalist aesthetics.
Framework Agnostic Concepts: Focuses on core design taste that can be applied across different web frameworks and libraries.

useCases.description: Generate wireframes and prototypes that are immediately presentable to stakeholders without requiring a manual design pass.

useCases.title: Low-code Customization
useCases.description: Enhance low-code platform generation capabilities by ensuring the raw output adheres to modern aesthetic standards.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers, designers, and 'vibecoders' who use AI tools to generate frontend code. It is for anyone frustrated by the generic, unpolished look of standard LLM-generated user interfaces.
